## File: README.md

# mgpl-diagnostics/.github

Organisation-wide files for [github.com/mgpl-diagnostics](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics).

- `profile/README.md` is the organisation's profile page.
- `profile/banner.svg` is generated by `scripts/make-banner.mjs`. Text is converted to vector paths from the
  Manrope font, and the logo comes from report-kit. Run the script inside the local MGPL workspace.
- `profile/avatar.png` is the organisation's profile picture, generated by `scripts/make-avatar.mjs` (the logo's drop
  icon on the banner's navy). GitHub has no API for it: upload it in the org settings → Profile.
- `scripts/protect-repos.mjs` applies the repository rules to every repo (PR-only `main`, required CI and
  code-owner review, maintainer-only release tags, private vulnerability reporting). Re-run it after creating
  or publishing a repo: `node scripts/protect-repos.mjs` (add `--dry-run` to preview).
- `.github/` holds the default community files every repo inherits: issue forms, PR template, CONTRIBUTING,
  SECURITY, CODE_OF_CONDUCT and SUPPORT.


---

## File: .github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

# Code of Conduct

We want MGPL Diagnostics to be a welcoming place for everyone, whatever their experience, background or
identity.

## Expected

- Be respectful and assume good intent.
- Give and take feedback on the work, not the person.
- Respect privacy: never share anyone's personal or medical information.

## Not acceptable

- Harassment, insults, or discriminatory language.
- Publishing others' private information, including patient data.
- Sustained disruption of issues, pull requests or discussions.

## Enforcement

Maintainers may edit or remove comments, lock threads, or block people who break these rules.
Report problems privately to the maintainers through a repository's **Security → Report a vulnerability**
form (mark it as a conduct report), or use GitHub's **Report content** option.

Adapted from the [Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct/), version 2.1.

## File: .github/CONTRIBUTING.md

# Contributing to MGPL Diagnostics

Thanks for helping. These rules apply to every repository in
[mgpl-diagnostics](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics) unless a repo says otherwise.

## The one rule: fork → branch → pull request

Nobody pushes to `main`, maintainers included. Every change, however small, arrives as a pull request
from a fork and is merged only after review and green CI.

```bash
# 1. Fork and clone (GitHub CLI)
gh repo fork mgpl-diagnostics/report-kit --clone
cd report-kit

# 2. Branch
git switch -c fix/lft-unit-wrap

# 3. Change, then run the checks the repo's AGENTS.md lists
npm install
npm run typecheck
npm run smoke            # report-kit / invoice-kit

# 4. Push to YOUR fork and open the PR against mgpl-diagnostics/<repo>:main
git push -u origin fix/lft-unit-wrap
gh pr create --fill
```

Keep your fork current with `gh repo sync` (or `git fetch upstream && git rebase upstream/main`).

## What `main` enforces

| Rule | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Pull request required | No direct pushes, no force-pushes, no branch deletion |
| 1 approving review from a code owner | Someone who knows the renderer signs off |
| New commits dismiss earlier approvals | What gets merged is what was reviewed |
| CI must pass (`ci`) | Typecheck, build and smoke tests on every PR |
| All conversations resolved | Nothing slips through |
| Squash merge only, linear history | One clean commit per PR |
| Release tags `v*` are maintainer-only | Tags publish packages |

Workflows from first-time and outside contributors wait for a maintainer's approval before they run.

## Before you open a PR

- **Open an issue first** for anything larger than a small fix, so we can agree on the approach.
- **PR title = commit message.** Use `type(scope): summary`, e.g. `feat(invoice-kit): add UPI reference field`.
  Types: `feat`, `fix`, `data`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`.
- **Visual changes need before/after screenshots** of the PDF or HTML.
- **HTTP contract changes** touch two repos: the kit and `client` (its `src/types.ts` mirrors the kits).
  Open both PRs and link them.
- **Test data** (reference ranges, units, prices) must cite a source in the PR.

## Privacy — non-negotiable

These repos are public. A PR is rejected, and its history may be rewritten, if it contains:

- real patient names, phone numbers, ages, IDs, or report/invoice PDFs from real patients;
- real signatures or stamps;
- secrets, tokens, or `.env` files.

Use the built-in samples or made-up data. Real signatures load at runtime from env vars
(`MGPL_SIGNATURE_*`) and never live in git.

## Licence of contributions

The code is **source-available, all rights reserved** (see each repo's `LICENSE`). You may fork on GitHub to
propose changes; that does not grant a licence to use the code elsewhere.

By opening a pull request you confirm the work is your own (or you have the right to submit it), and you
agree that MGPL Diagnostics may use, modify and distribute it under the repository's licence terms.

## Getting help

- Bugs and features: open an issue using the templates.
- Security problems: **don't** open an issue. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).
- Be kind: [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

## File: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml

```yaml
name: Bug report
description: Something renders wrong, crashes, or returns the wrong result.
title: "bug: "
labels: ["bug", "triage"]
body:
  - type: markdown
    attributes:
      value: |
        Thanks for taking the time to report this.

        > [!CAUTION]
        > **Never paste real patient data.** No names, phone numbers, ages tied to a person, report PDFs from real patients, or signatures. Use the built-in samples or made-up values. Issues are public and indexed.

  - type: dropdown
    id: repo
    attributes:
      label: Package or app
      options:
        - report-kit
        - invoice-kit
        - client
        - report-studio
        - website
        - other / not sure
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: input
    id: version
    attributes:
      label: Version
      description: From package.json, or the commit SHA.
      placeholder: "2.0.0"
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: dropdown
    id: runtime
    attributes:
      label: Where does it run?
      multiple: true
      options:
        - Next.js
        - Fastify
        - Express / node:http
        - Hono / Bun / Deno
        - Browser (client SDK)
        - Other
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: textarea
    id: what-happened
    attributes:
      label: What happened?
      description: Include error messages and screenshots of the PDF or HTML if it's visual.
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: textarea
    id: expected
    attributes:
      label: What did you expect?
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: textarea
    id: repro
    attributes:
      label: Steps or request to reproduce
      description: The smallest request body or code that shows the problem (with fictional data).
      render: ts
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: input
    id: node
    attributes:
      label: Node.js version and OS
      placeholder: "Node 22.11, Ubuntu 24.04"

  - type: checkboxes
    id: privacy
    attributes:
      label: Privacy
      options:
        - label: This issue contains no real patient data, contact details or signatures.
          required: true
```

    id: contribute
    attributes:

      value: |

  - type: input
    id: test
    attributes:
      label: Test or profile
      placeholder: "LFT — Liver Function Test"

      required: true

    id: parameter

    validations:

      label: Proposed value
      description: Include sex / age splits if they apply.
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: input
    id: source
    attributes:
      label: Source

## File: .github/SECURITY.md

# Security policy

MGPL Diagnostics software produces medical reports and patient bills, so we treat security reports seriously.

## Reporting a vulnerability

**Do not open a public issue.** Report it privately:

1. Open the affected repository on GitHub.
2. Go to **Security → Report a vulnerability**.
3. Describe the issue, how to reproduce it, and its impact.

Only the maintainers can see the report. We aim to acknowledge it within **3 days** and to agree a fix
and disclosure timeline with you.

## What counts

- Anything that could expose patient data, or let someone alter a report or invoice.
- Path traversal, injection, or request-size / DoS issues in the HTTP handlers.
- Real patient data, signatures or secrets accidentally committed to any repo or package.
- Supply-chain problems in our workflows or published packages.

## Supported versions

The latest major release of each package receives security fixes.

## File: .github/SUPPORT.md

# Support

- **Read the docs first.** Each repo has a README, `docs/api.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `llms.txt`.
- **Found a bug or want a feature?** Open an issue using a template.
- **Wrong reference range, unit or price?** Use the *Test data correction* template and cite a source.
- **Security problem?** See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). Never use a public issue.

Please never include real patient data in issues, discussions or pull requests.

## Checklist

- [ ] `npm run typecheck` passes
- [ ] The repo's tests pass (`npm run smoke`, `npm run test:api`, or `npm run build` — see its AGENTS.md)
- [ ] Docs updated (README, `docs/api.md`, AGENTS.md, llms.txt) if behaviour or API changed
- [ ] HTTP contract changed? `client` types updated in a linked PR
- [ ] **No real patient data, contact details or signatures** in code, tests, fixtures or screenshots

## File: llms.txt

# mgpl-diagnostics/.github

> Organisation-wide files for MGPL Diagnostics (Maa Gayatri Path Lab, Arang, Raipur): the GitHub profile page and banner, the community files every repo inherits (issue forms, PR template, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, SUPPORT), and scripts that generate the banner and avatar and apply the repository rules.

Key facts for agents:
- Every repo is public; `main` takes pull requests only (from forks for outside contributors), with green `ci` and a code-owner review. Rules are applied by `node scripts/protect-repos.mjs`.
- GraphQL first across the org; REST only for binary downloads, assets, health checks and webhooks.
- Never commit patient data, real signatures, secrets or `.env` files.

## Repos

- [db-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/db-kit): data layer (MongoDB/PostgreSQL, ACID, storage for books and finance, Redis cache)
- [auth-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/auth-kit): passwords, sessions, roles (internal API)
- [catalog-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/catalog-kit): tests, ranges, prices, search
- [report-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/report-kit): A4 lab reports (PDF + HTML)
- [invoice-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/invoice-kit): patient invoices (PDF + HTML)
- [client](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/client): headless frontend SDK (a typed method for every GraphQL operation)
- [report-studio](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/report-studio): reference Next.js app
- [website](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/website): the lab's public website
- [finance-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/finance-kit): GST and GSTR-1/3B data, receivables and credit notes, partner settlements with TDS, cash/bank, lock dates, year-end; posts through ledger-kit
- [ledger-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/ledger-kit): our own accounting engine: groups, ledgers, vouchers, automatic posting (db-kit PostingHook), books reports; no Tally import/export
- [api](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/api): the backend, one GraphQL endpoint (`POST /graphql`, Yoga on Fastify) over every kit
- [security-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/security-kit): device signals bound to sessions, client IP behind proxies, TLS fingerprint, security/CORS headers, log redaction (browser + server, zero dependencies)
- [mail-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/mail-kit): mails in our own mail design language, compiled to email-safe HTML + text; SMTP, sent through the worker queue when available
- [worker-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/worker-kit): background jobs on BullMQ (Redis), in-process, or worker-with-fallback; same retries and results everywhere
- [pgbouncer-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/pgbouncer-kit) (in progress): PgBouncer in front of PostgreSQL for api replicas: config, user list, compose service, health checks, TLS (transaction pooling)
- Coming soon: lab-panel, auth client, and more kits

## Files

- [profile/README.md](profile/README.md): the organisation profile
- [.github/CONTRIBUTING.md](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md): fork → branch → pull request
- [.github/SECURITY.md](.github/SECURITY.md): private vulnerability reporting
- [scripts/protect-repos.mjs](scripts/protect-repos.mjs): rulesets and repo settings
- [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt): every file in one document

### 🧱 Backend kits

<table>
<tr>
<td width="50%" valign="top">

#### [db-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/db-kit) &nbsp;`data`
Patients, bookings, samples, reports, invoices and payments on **MongoDB or PostgreSQL**, behind one API.
Workflows are ACID on both. Stores the books and the finance records, and includes a Redis cache
toolkit.

</td>
<td width="50%" valign="top">

#### [auth-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/auth-kit) &nbsp;`auth`
scrypt passwords and revocable sessions, plus timing-safe, rate-limited login and single-use reset
links. Roles and permissions work per branch, for a multi-branch lab.

</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td width="50%" valign="top">

#### [catalog-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/catalog-kit) &nbsp;`data`
614 tests, each with parameters, units, methods, reference ranges, sample types and prices. Fuzzy search
(~30 µs) understands lab shorthand: *lft*, *kft*, *sgpt*, *fbs*, *vit d*.

</td>
<td width="50%" valign="top">

#### [report-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/report-kit) · [invoice-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/invoice-kit) &nbsp;`render`
A4 lab reports and patient invoices as PDF, rendered in pure Node.js, with matching HTML. Letterhead,
barcode, QR and GST bills accurate to the paisa.

</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td width="50%" valign="top">

#### [ledger-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/ledger-kit) &nbsp;`books`
Our own accounting engine: the 28 standard account groups, ledgers and vouchers, numbered per financial
year and always balanced. Invoices and payments post themselves, and lock dates hold. Trial balance, day
book, P&L and balance sheet, proven identical on MongoDB and PostgreSQL.

</td>
<td width="50%" valign="top">

#### [finance-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/finance-kit) &nbsp;`money`
GST by place of supply with GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B data, B2B receivables and credit notes, and
collection-centre settlements with TDS. Also day-end cash, bank reconciliation, lock dates, year-end
close and CSV exports for the CA.

</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2" valign="top">

#### [security-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/security-kit) &nbsp;`security`
One package for both sides. Frontends collect a device id, a per-tab id and a coarse fingerprint; the
backend binds them to the session and stops a token used from another browser. Also client IP behind
proxies, security and CORS headers, and log redaction. Zero dependencies.

</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2" valign="top">

#### [mail-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/mail-kit) &nbsp;`mail`
Mails written in our own mail design language instead of HTML, compiled to email-safe HTML and plain
text in one design. Sent through the worker's queue when it is running, or straight over SMTP when it
is not. Zero dependencies.

</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2" valign="top">

#### [worker-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/worker-kit) &nbsp;`jobs`
Background jobs defined once and run on BullMQ over Redis by a separate worker, in-process when there
is no Redis, or on the worker when it is up and standalone when it is not. Same retries, results and
error messages everywhere.

</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2" valign="top">

#### [pgbouncer-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/pgbouncer-kit) &nbsp;`scaling` &nbsp;*in progress*
PgBouncer in front of PostgreSQL, so every api replica shares one small pool of database connections.
It will generate the PgBouncer config and user list, a compose service, health checks and TLS settings
for transaction pooling, tested against real PostgreSQL and PgBouncer.

</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2" valign="top">

#### …and many more &nbsp;`on the way`
Each new kit does one job well and plugs into the same GraphQL API. Watch this organisation
for what ships next.

</td>
</tr>
</table>

### 🖥️ Apps and clients

| | |
| --- | --- |
| [**api**](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/api) `backend` | The backend: one GraphQL endpoint on Fastify that combines every kit |
| [**client**](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/client) `frontend` | Headless, typed, zero-dependency SDK with a method for every GraphQL operation. Bring your own UI |
| [**website**](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/website) `site` | The lab's public website: a living 3D lab, the full test catalogue with prices, home collection and booking |
| [**report-studio**](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/report-studio) `app` | Reference Next.js app: report and invoice designer, result entry |
| **lab-panel** `coming soon` | Registrations, samples, results, billing and books for every branch |
| **auth client** `coming soon` | Sign-in for frontends, with adapters for TanStack Query and others |

### 🧭 How it fits together

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Apps
    P[lab panel]
    S[report-studio]
    W[website]
  end
  Apps -->|"GraphQL"| API["api<br/>Fastify · GraphQL Yoga"]
  API --> AUTH[auth-kit]
  API --> DB[db-kit]
  API --> CAT[catalog-kit]
  API --> RND["report-kit · invoice-kit"]
  API --> FIN[finance-kit]
  API --> SEC[security-kit]
  API --> MAIL[mail-kit]
  MAIL --> JOBS[worker-kit]
  FIN --> BOOKS[ledger-kit]
  BOOKS --> DB
  FIN --> DB
  DB --> M[(MongoDB)]
  DB --> PGB["PgBouncer<br/>pgbouncer-kit"]
  PGB --> PG[(PostgreSQL)]
  DB --> R[(Redis)]
  AUTH --> R
  JOBS --> R
  RND --> PDF["A4 PDF / HTML<br/>inside the GraphQL response"]
```

**One endpoint.** Everything goes through `POST /graphql`, PDFs included (as base64). The only other route
is a health check.

### ⚡ A taste

```ts
import { createMgplGraphQLClient, documentBlob, openBlob } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/client";

const mgpl = createMgplGraphQLClient({ url: "https://api.your-lab.in/graphql" });
await mgpl.auth.login({ email: "desk@your-lab.in", password });

const patient = await mgpl.patients.register({ branchId, name: "Kavita Sharma", sex: "female", ageYears: 32 });
const invoice = await mgpl.invoices.issue({
  branchId, patientId: patient.id,
  items: [{ code: "CBC" }],                          // name and MRP from the catalog
  payments: [{ amountPaise: 30000, mode: "upi" }],
});
// → numbered per branch and financial year, Sales + Receipt vouchers posted, books still balance

openBlob(documentBlob(await mgpl.documents.invoice(invoice.id)));  // the A4 PDF, as base64 over GraphQL
```

### ✅ How we work

- **Money is exact.** Integer paise, double-entry vouchers that must balance, and ACID transactions on
  MongoDB and PostgreSQL. Tests show two concurrent overpayments can't both succeed.
- **Both databases, one contract.** The same test suite runs on real MongoDB and real PostgreSQL.
- **Secure by default.** Tokens are stored only as hashes. Data is isolated per organisation, and
  permissions are checked per branch.
- **HTML and PDF match.** One geometry, one row model, the same page breaks; every value is checked inside the PDF.
- **No patient data in any repo.** Real signatures load at runtime from the server and are never committed.
- **Docs for people and AI.** Every repo has a README, `AGENTS.md` and `llms.txt`.
- **Reviewed, always.** Nobody pushes to `main`. Every change is a pull request from a fork, with green
  CI and a code-owner review. [How to contribute →](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/.github/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md)

<p align="center"><sub>© MGPL Diagnostics (Maa Gayatri Path Lab), Arang, Raipur. Code is published for reference; all rights reserved.</sub></p>

## File: scripts/llms-full.mjs

````js
// Builds llms-full.txt: every doc and source file of the repo in one plain-text document for AI tools.
//   node scripts/llms-full.mjs "<title>" <file-or-folder> [file-or-folder …]
// Folders are walked recursively. Output order: README, AGENTS, docs, then the rest alphabetically.
// Skipped: build output, dependencies, lockfiles, generated files, binaries. Files over 150 KB are
// listed (path + size) instead of inlined. CI checks the file is up to date (`npm run llms` + git diff).
import { readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { extname, join, relative } from "node:path";

const [title, ...inputs] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (!title || !inputs.length) {
  console.error('usage: node scripts/llms-full.mjs "<title>" <file-or-folder> …');
  process.exit(1);
}

const TEXT = new Set([".ts", ".tsx", ".mts", ".cts", ".js", ".mjs", ".cjs", ".md", ".mdx", ".json", ".css", ".yml", ".yaml", ".txt", ".graphql", ".gql", ".sql", ".html"]);
const SKIP_DIRS = new Set(["node_modules", "dist", ".next", ".git", ".turbo", "coverage", "examples", ".pg-test"]);
const SKIP_FILES = /(^|\/)(package-lock\.json|pnpm-lock\.yaml|yarn\.lock|llms-full\.txt|[^/]*\.generated\.[^/]+|[^/]*\.log)$/;
const MAX = 150 * 1024;
const LANG = { ".ts": "ts", ".tsx": "tsx", ".mts": "ts", ".cts": "ts", ".js": "js", ".mjs": "js", ".cjs": "js", ".json": "json", ".css": "css", ".yml": "yaml", ".yaml": "yaml", ".graphql": "graphql", ".gql": "graphql", ".sql": "sql", ".html": "html" };

const posix = (p) => p.split("\\").join("/");
const files = new Set();
function walk(p) {
  const st = statSync(p);
  if (st.isDirectory()) {
    for (const name of readdirSync(p)) if (!SKIP_DIRS.has(name)) walk(join(p, name));
  } else if (TEXT.has(extname(p).toLowerCase()) && !SKIP_FILES.test(posix(p))) {
    files.add(posix(relative(".", p)));
  }
}
for (const input of inputs) walk(input);

const rank = (f) => (/^README\.md$/i.test(f) ? 0 : /^AGENTS\.md$/i.test(f) ? 1 : /^docs\//.test(f) ? 2 : 3);
const ordered = [...files].sort((a, b) => rank(a) - rank(b) || (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0));

const parts = [`# ${title} — full documentation and source\n\n> Generated by scripts/llms-full.mjs. Do not edit by hand. ${ordered.length} files.\n\n## Contents\n\n${ordered.map((f) => `- ${f}`).join("\n")}\n`];
const omitted = [];
for (const f of ordered) {
  // LF-normalised text, so Windows and Linux checkouts produce byte-identical output
  const body = readFileSync(f, "utf8").replace(/\r\n/g, "\n").trim();
  const size = Buffer.byteLength(body);
  if (size > MAX) {
    omitted.push(`${f} (${(size / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB)`);
    parts.push(`\n\n---\n\n## File: ${f}\n\n_Omitted: ${(size / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB. Read the file directly._\n`);
    continue;
  }
  const lang = LANG[extname(f).toLowerCase()];
  const fence = body.includes("```") ? "````" : "```";
  parts.push(`\n\n---\n\n## File: ${f}\n\n${lang ? `${fence}${lang}\n${body}\n${fence}` : body}\n`);
}
const out = parts.join("");
writeFileSync("llms-full.txt", out);
console.log(`llms-full.txt: ${ordered.length} files, ${(out.length / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB${omitted.length ? `; omitted (too large): ${omitted.join(", ")}` : ""}`);
````

## File: scripts/make-avatar.mjs

```js
// Builds profile/avatar.svg + profile/avatar.png (1024 × 1024) — the organisation's profile picture.
// The logo's drop icon in white on the banner's navy gradient. GitHub has no API for org avatars:
// upload avatar.png at github.com/organizations/mgpl-diagnostics/settings/profile.
// Run inside the MGPL workspace:  node org-profile/scripts/make-avatar.mjs
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { dirname, join } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { Resvg } from "@resvg/resvg-js";

const here = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const ws = join(here, "..", "..");
const NAVY = "#14264A", DEEP = "#0C1A35", SAFFRON = "#C2410C", GOLD = "#E9A23B", WHITE = "#FFFFFF";

// the logo's <g id="icon"> (drop + lotus + dot), drop recoloured white
const logo = readFileSync(join(ws, "report-kit", "assets", "report-assets", "logo.svg"), "utf8");
const icon = logo.match(/<g id="icon">([\s\S]*?)<\/g>/)[1].replace(/#14264A/gi, WHITE);

// icon bounds in logo units: x 84–316, y 92–432 (centre 200, 262)
const S = 1024, scale = 1.9, cx = 200, cy = 262;
const tx = S / 2 - cx * scale, ty = S / 2 - cy * scale;

const svg = `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="${S}" height="${S}" viewBox="0 0 ${S} ${S}" role="img" aria-label="MGPL Diagnostics">
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="bg" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="1"><stop offset="0" stop-color="${NAVY}"/><stop offset="1" stop-color="${DEEP}"/></linearGradient>
    <radialGradient id="glowA" cx="0.5" cy="0.5" r="0.5"><stop offset="0" stop-color="${SAFFRON}" stop-opacity="0.42"/><stop offset="1" stop-color="${SAFFRON}" stop-opacity="0"/></radialGradient>
    <radialGradient id="glowB" cx="0.5" cy="0.5" r="0.5"><stop offset="0" stop-color="${GOLD}" stop-opacity="0.22"/><stop offset="1" stop-color="${GOLD}" stop-opacity="0"/></radialGradient>
  </defs>
  <rect width="${S}" height="${S}" fill="url(#bg)"/>
  <circle cx="${S * 0.82}" cy="${S * 0.9}" r="${S * 0.55}" fill="url(#glowA)"/>
  <circle cx="${S * 0.12}" cy="${S * 0.05}" r="${S * 0.45}" fill="url(#glowB)"/>
  <g transform="translate(${tx.toFixed(1)} ${ty.toFixed(1)}) scale(${scale})">${icon}</g>
</svg>
`;
const out = join(here, "..", "profile");
writeFileSync(join(out, "avatar.svg"), svg);
writeFileSync(join(out, "avatar.png"), new Resvg(svg, { fitTo: { mode: "width", value: S } }).render().asPng());
console.log("profile/avatar.svg + profile/avatar.png (1024 × 1024)");
```

## File: scripts/make-banner.mjs

```js
// Builds profile/banner.svg — dark navy hero with the logo in white, a 96-well test-plate motif,
// and repo chips. All text is converted to vector paths (fontkit + Manrope), so it renders the
// same on every machine. Run inside the MGPL workspace:  node org-profile/scripts/make-banner.mjs
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { dirname, join } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import * as fontkit from "fontkit";

const here = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const ws = join(here, "..", "..");
const fontsDir = join(ws, "report-kit", "assets", "report-fonts");
const font = (w) => fontkit.openSync(join(fontsDir, `manrope-${w}.woff`));
const F = { 500: font(500), 600: font(600), 700: font(700), 800: font(800) };

const NAVY = "#14264A", DEEP = "#0C1A35", SAFFRON = "#C2410C", GOLD = "#E9A23B", MIST = "#C8D0E0", WHITE = "#FFFFFF";

// fontkit (react-pdf's font engine): shaping with kerning, and glyph outlines without opentype.js's NaN points
function measure(str, size, weight, spacing = 0) {
  const f = F[weight];
  const run = f.layout(str);
  return run.positions.reduce((a, p) => a + p.xAdvance, 0) * (size / f.unitsPerEm) + spacing * (run.glyphs.length - 1);
}
/** text → <path> (outlines in font units, flipped and scaled into place) */
function text(str, { x, y, size, weight = 800, fill = WHITE, spacing = 0, anchor = "start", opacity }) {
  const f = F[weight];
  const s = size / f.unitsPerEm;
  const run = f.layout(str);
  let cx = anchor === "middle" ? x - measure(str, size, weight, spacing) / 2 : x;
  let d = "";
  run.glyphs.forEach((g, i) => {
    const p = run.positions[i];
    const ox = cx + p.xOffset * s, oy = y - p.yOffset * s;
    d += g.path.mapPoints((px, py) => [ox + px * s, oy - py * s]).toSVG();
    cx += p.xAdvance * s + spacing;
  });
  if (d.includes("NaN")) throw new Error(`NaN in outline for "${str}"`);
  return `<path fill="${fill}"${opacity ? ` opacity="${opacity}"` : ""} d="${d}"/>`;
}
/** rounded chip with label */
function chip(label, x, y, { fill = "rgba(255,255,255,0.08)", stroke = "rgba(255,255,255,0.22)", color = WHITE, dot } = {}) {
  const size = 15, padX = 16, h = 34;
  const w = measure(label, size, 700) + padX * 2 + (dot ? 16 : 0);
  return {
    w,
    svg: `<rect x="${x}" y="${y}" width="${w.toFixed(1)}" height="${h}" rx="17" fill="${fill}" stroke="${stroke}"/>` +
      (dot ? `<circle cx="${x + padX + 4}" cy="${y + h / 2}" r="4.5" fill="${dot}"/>` : "") +
      text(label, { x: x + padX + (dot ? 16 : 0), y: y + 22.5, size, weight: 700, fill: color }),
  };
}

// logo recoloured for a dark background
const logo = readFileSync(join(ws, "report-kit", "assets", "report-assets", "logo.svg"), "utf8")
  .replace(/^[\s\S]*?<svg[^>]*>/, "")
  .replace(/<\/svg>\s*$/, "")
  .replace(/<title>[\s\S]*?<\/title>/, "")
  .replace(/#14264A/gi, WHITE)
  .replace(/#675F54/gi, MIST);

const W = 1280, H = 420;

// 96-well plate (8 × 12) whose lit wells form a rising chart — the org keeps growing
const plateX = 905, plateY = 66, pitch = 26, r = 9;
const heights = [1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8];
let wells = "";
for (let row = 0; row < 8; row++)
  for (let col = 0; col < 12; col++) {
    const cx = plateX + col * pitch, cy = plateY + row * pitch;
    const top = 8 - heights[col];
    const fill = row === top ? SAFFRON : row > top ? GOLD : null;
    const op = row > top ? (0.45 + 0.55 * (col / 11)).toFixed(2) : null;
    wells += fill
      ? `<circle cx="${cx}" cy="${cy}" r="${r}" fill="${fill}"${op && op !== "1.00" ? ` opacity="${op}"` : ""}/>`
      : `<circle cx="${cx}" cy="${cy}" r="${r}" fill="none" stroke="rgba(255,255,255,0.18)" stroke-width="1.5"/>`;
  }
const plateW = 11 * pitch + 2 * r + 28, plateH = 7 * pitch + 2 * r + 28;
const rowLabels = "ABCDEFGH".split("").map((L, i) => text(L, { x: plateX - 30, y: plateY + i * pitch + 5, size: 11, weight: 700, fill: MIST, opacity: 0.55 })).join("");
const colLabels = Array.from({ length: 12 }, (_, i) => text(String(i + 1), { x: plateX + i * pitch, y: plateY - 18, size: 11, weight: 700, fill: MIST, anchor: "middle", opacity: 0.55 })).join("");

// principle chips — deliberately not repo names, so the banner stays true as the org grows
let cx = 96;
const chips = [
  ["Public repos", GOLD],
  ["Typed APIs", GOLD],
  ["Headless by design", "#7DD3FC"],
  ["Runs anywhere", "#7DD3FC"],
  ["AI-agent ready", "#A7F3D0"],
]
  .map(([label, dot]) => {
    const c = chip(label, cx, 340, { dot });
    cx += c.w + 10;
    return c.svg;
  })
  .join("");

const svg = `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="${W}" height="${H}" viewBox="0 0 ${W} ${H}" role="img" aria-label="MGPL Diagnostics — building the future of diagnostic software, in public">
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="bg" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="1"><stop offset="0" stop-color="${NAVY}"/><stop offset="1" stop-color="${DEEP}"/></linearGradient>
    <radialGradient id="glowA" cx="0.5" cy="0.5" r="0.5"><stop offset="0" stop-color="${SAFFRON}" stop-opacity="0.45"/><stop offset="1" stop-color="${SAFFRON}" stop-opacity="0"/></radialGradient>
    <radialGradient id="glowB" cx="0.5" cy="0.5" r="0.5"><stop offset="0" stop-color="${GOLD}" stop-opacity="0.28"/><stop offset="1" stop-color="${GOLD}" stop-opacity="0"/></radialGradient>
    <pattern id="dots" width="22" height="22" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse"><circle cx="2" cy="2" r="1.2" fill="#FFFFFF" opacity="0.06"/></pattern>
    <linearGradient id="bar" x1="0" x2="1"><stop offset="0" stop-color="${SAFFRON}"/><stop offset="1" stop-color="${GOLD}"/></linearGradient>
    <clipPath id="round"><rect width="${W}" height="${H}" rx="20"/></clipPath>
  </defs>
  <g clip-path="url(#round)">
    <rect width="${W}" height="${H}" fill="url(#bg)"/>
    <rect width="${W}" height="${H}" fill="url(#dots)"/>
    <circle cx="1040" cy="380" r="330" fill="url(#glowA)"/>
    <circle cx="140" cy="-40" r="260" fill="url(#glowB)"/>

    <svg x="84" y="42" width="300" height="126" viewBox="60 68 920 388">${logo}</svg>

    ${text("Building the future", { x: 96, y: 222, size: 48, weight: 800 })}
    ${text("of diagnostic software.", { x: 96, y: 278, size: 48, weight: 800, fill: GOLD })}
    ${text("A growing family of public, modular repos for modern pathology labs.", { x: 98, y: 314, size: 17, weight: 600, fill: MIST, opacity: 0.85 })}
    ${chips}

    <g>
      <rect x="${plateX - 46}" y="${plateY - 40}" width="${plateW + 32}" height="${plateH + 26}" rx="22" fill="rgba(255,255,255,0.05)" stroke="rgba(255,255,255,0.14)"/>
      ${colLabels}${rowLabels}${wells}
    </g>
    ${text("BUILT IN PUBLIC", { x: plateX + 143, y: 322, size: 13, weight: 800, fill: GOLD, spacing: 3, anchor: "middle" })}
    ${text("Maa Gayatri Path Lab  ·  Arang, Raipur", { x: plateX + 143, y: 348, size: 14, weight: 600, fill: MIST, anchor: "middle", opacity: 0.75 })}

    <rect y="${H - 8}" width="${W}" height="8" fill="url(#bar)"/>
  </g>
</svg>
`;
writeFileSync(join(here, "..", "profile", "banner.svg"), svg);
console.log(`profile/banner.svg  ${(svg.length / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB`);
```

## File: scripts/protect-repos.mjs

```js
// Applies the org's repository rules to every repo (or the ones named), idempotently.
//
//   node scripts/protect-repos.mjs              # all repos in the org
//   node scripts/protect-repos.mjs report-kit   # just these
//   node scripts/protect-repos.mjs --dry-run    # print what would be sent
//
// Needs the GitHub CLI logged in as an org owner (scopes: repo). On the Free plan GitHub enforces
// rulesets only on PUBLIC repos, so private repos are skipped with a warning.
//
// What it sets (see .github/CONTRIBUTING.md for the contributor-facing version):
//   • ruleset "main": PR required (1 code-owner approval, stale approvals dismissed, last push approved,
//     threads resolved, squash only), CI check "ci" required where the repo has CI, linear history,
//     no force-push, no deletion. Org admins may only bypass THROUGH a pull request, so nobody can
//     push to main directly.
//   • ruleset "release tags": only org admins create, move or delete v* tags (tags publish packages).
//   • repo settings: squash merge only, PR title as commit, delete branches on merge, no wiki.
//   • private vulnerability reporting on; workflows default to read-only tokens; workflows from
//     every outside contributor wait for approval.
// Contributors without write access must fork; the org's base permission is "read", so that
// includes org members.
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";

const ORG = "mgpl-diagnostics";
const DRY = process.argv.includes("--dry-run");
const only = process.argv.slice(2).filter((a) => !a.startsWith("--"));

// Required status checks per repo (job ids in .github/workflows/ci.yml). Repos without CI get none.
const CHECKS = {
  "report-kit": ["ci"], "invoice-kit": ["ci"], client: ["ci"], "report-studio": ["ci"],
  "catalog-kit": ["ci"], "db-kit": ["ci"], "auth-kit": ["ci"], "finance-kit": ["ci"], "ledger-kit": ["ci"], api: ["ci"], "security-kit": ["ci"], "mail-kit": ["ci"], "worker-kit": ["ci"],
};
const GITHUB_ACTIONS_APP_ID = 15368;

function gh(args, body) {
  if (DRY && body !== undefined) {
    console.log(`  [dry-run] gh ${args.join(" ")}\n${JSON.stringify(body, null, 2).replace(/^/gm, "    ")}`);
    return null;
  }
  const out = execFileSync("gh", ["api", ...args, ...(body !== undefined ? ["--input", "-"] : [])], {
    input: body !== undefined ? JSON.stringify(body) : undefined,
    encoding: "utf8",
    stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"],
  });
  return out.trim() ? JSON.parse(out) : null;
}
function step(label, fn) {
  try {
    fn();
    console.log(`  ✓ ${label}`);
  } catch (e) {
    console.log(`  ✗ ${label}: ${(e.stderr || e.message).toString().trim().split("\n")[0]}`);
    process.exitCode = 1;
  }
}

function mainRuleset(repo) {
  const checks = CHECKS[repo] ?? [];
  return {
    name: "main",
    target: "branch",
    enforcement: "active",
    conditions: { ref_name: { include: ["~DEFAULT_BRANCH"], exclude: [] } },
    bypass_actors: [{ actor_type: "OrganizationAdmin", actor_id: 1, bypass_mode: "pull_request" }],
    rules: [
      { type: "deletion" },
      { type: "non_fast_forward" },
      { type: "required_linear_history" },
      {
        type: "pull_request",
        parameters: {
          required_approving_review_count: 1,
          dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push: true,
          require_code_owner_review: true,
          require_last_push_approval: true,
          required_review_thread_resolution: true,
          allowed_merge_methods: ["squash"],
        },
      },
      ...(checks.length
        ? [{
            type: "required_status_checks",
            parameters: {
              strict_required_status_checks_policy: true,
              required_status_checks: checks.map((context) => ({ context, integration_id: GITHUB_ACTIONS_APP_ID })),
            },
          }]
        : []),
    ],
  };
}
const tagRuleset = {
  name: "release tags",
  target: "tag",
  enforcement: "active",
  conditions: { ref_name: { include: ["refs/tags/v*"], exclude: [] } },
  bypass_actors: [{ actor_type: "OrganizationAdmin", actor_id: 1, bypass_mode: "always" }],
  rules: [{ type: "creation" }, { type: "update" }, { type: "deletion" }, { type: "non_fast_forward" }],
};

function upsertRuleset(repo, rs) {
  const existing = DRY ? [] : gh([`repos/${ORG}/${repo}/rulesets`]) ?? [];
  const found = existing.find((r) => r.name === rs.name && r.source_type === "Repository");
  if (found) gh(["-X", "PUT", `repos/${ORG}/${repo}/rulesets/${found.id}`], rs);
  else gh(["-X", "POST", `repos/${ORG}/${repo}/rulesets`], rs);
}

const repos = gh(["--paginate", `orgs/${ORG}/repos?per_page=100`]).filter((r) => !r.archived);
for (const r of repos) {
  if (only.length && !only.includes(r.name)) continue;
  console.log(`\n${r.name} (${r.visibility}, ${r.default_branch})`);
  if (r.visibility !== "public") {
    console.log("  – skipped: rulesets on private repos need a paid plan. Make it public, then re-run.");
    continue;
  }
  step("merge settings", () =>
    gh(["-X", "PATCH", `repos/${ORG}/${r.name}`], {
      allow_squash_merge: true,
      allow_merge_commit: false,
      allow_rebase_merge: false,
      squash_merge_commit_title: "PR_TITLE",
      squash_merge_commit_message: "PR_BODY",
      delete_branch_on_merge: true,
      allow_update_branch: true,
      has_wiki: false,
    }));
  step(`ruleset "main"${CHECKS[r.name] ? ` (checks: ${CHECKS[r.name].join(", ")})` : ""}`, () => upsertRuleset(r.name, mainRuleset(r.name)));
  step('ruleset "release tags"', () => upsertRuleset(r.name, tagRuleset));
  step("private vulnerability reporting", () => gh(["-X", "PUT", `repos/${ORG}/${r.name}/private-vulnerability-reporting`], {}));
  step("workflow token read-only", () =>
    gh(["-X", "PUT", `repos/${ORG}/${r.name}/actions/permissions/workflow`], {
      default_workflow_permissions: "read",
      can_approve_pull_request_reviews: false,
    }));
  step("approve workflows from all outside contributors", () =>
    gh(["-X", "PUT", `repos/${ORG}/${r.name}/actions/permissions/fork-pr-contributor-approval`], {
      approval_policy: "all_external_contributors",
    }));
}
```
